# Why Durgā is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *durga*. This is the file on how **Durgā** replaced it.

Durgā's mythology reaches its classic form in the Devī-Māhātmya, the 'Glory of the Goddess' embedded in the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa. There she appears when the gods are defeated and the demons rule heaven, earth, and the underworld. The buffalo-demon Mahiṣāsura had conquered the gods through austerities and battle.  Neither Brahmā, Viṣṇu, nor Śiva could defeat him alone.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Durgā
- **ASCII form:** durga
- **Meaning:** "'The Inaccessible One' — the warrior goddess, daughter of Himavat and consort of Śiva, slayer of the buffalo-demon Mahiṣa"
- **Domain of influence:** Protection, Strength, War
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** दुर्गा
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 71 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Durgā** to *durga* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → ā** — Macron: long /aː/: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

None of these marks is decoration. Each one is a fact about how the name was spoken, and each one is checkable against the scholarly record the temple cites.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Durgā** lives at [/sites/durga/](/sites/durga/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/durga/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/durga/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/durga/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Durgā** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Defense, Military & Security** — Born from the combined radiance of the gods to slay the buffalo-demon — the fortress no enemy can reach.
- **Insurance & Protection Services** — Protection personified; the fortress goddess.
- **Sports, Fitness & Competition** — Strength and protection; the warrior goddess of the arena.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Sanskrit tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Rig Veda](/texts/rig-veda/) and [Ramayana](/texts/ramayana/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
